attributes.cardDescription: Score the library against a record and link the best public matches.
attributes.readMe:
## What it is
Deterministic weighted keyword overlap. Anything under the floor is dropped rather than padded to three, and only **public** articles get linked, because a linked article is one an agent may paste to a customer.

## Three usages
1. **ServiceDesk** — the workspace suggestion panel.
2. **A self-service portal** — same scoring, run against the submitted description before the form is sent.
3. **An internal SOP finder** — scoring a runbook library against an alert description.

## The linked example
`../Incident/1234-dashboard-access` links the two articles this command scored highest against its SSO symptoms.

## Non-goals
Not semantic search. It is keyword overlap; a question phrased with entirely different vocabulary will not match, and that gap is reported rather than hidden.

**Open question.** Scoring is keyword overlap; see the article Spec. Same open question, same missing block.

## Why the example is a linked card
A command has no renderable instance, so `containedExamples` cannot hold one. The linked card is the command's natural target — open it and the effects described above are visible in its state and its conversation.

## Why not an LLM
Support teams judge these suggestions dozens of times a day. A wrong-but-explainable score survives that scrutiny; a black box does not — and a panel that goes blank when credits run out is worse than an approximate one.
